Pa1.technologies.wind.definition: Wind power, whether onshore or offshore.
Pa1.technologies.hydrogen.definition: Hydrogen used as an energy carrier, especially low-carbon, renewable or green hydrogen. Document the production pathway when the text identifies one.
Pa1.technologies.nuclear.definition: Counted as a low-carbon COMPARATOR, even though it is not a renewable technology.
Pa1.technologies.other_renewable.definition: Hydropower, bioenergy, geothermal, and marine energy.
Pa1.technologies.storage.definition: Statements in which batteries, pumped hydro, and other storage constitute the SUBJECT.
Pa1.frame_elements.F1a.fires_when: The paragraph refers to the monetary cost or price of the technology, of the electricity it generates, or of the bills, levies or taxes people pay as a result of it. Includes claims that it is cheap, expensive, cheaper or more costly than something else, or that costs are going up or down.
Pa1.frame_elements.F1a.does_not_fire_when: A figure is mentioned that does not represent a price. Installed capacity measured in megawatts, output expressed in terawatt-hours, or a tally of turbines is NOT a cost claim.
Pa1.frame_elements.F1b.fires_when: This paragraph refers to subsidies, feed-in tariffs, levies, auctions, public funding, tax credits, or the issue of who bears the cost of deployment.
Pa1.frame_elements.F2b.fires_when: The paragraph refers to investment, industrial capacity, decisions about factories or projects, exports, supply chains, or national competitiveness.
Pa1.frame_elements.F2b.does_not_fire_when: A company is only mentioned by name, or standard corporate boilerplate is present, while the statement does not bear on the technology.
Pa1.frame_elements.F2c.fires_when: The paragraph presents a deployment, output or market figure AS GROWTH, AS A RECORD, or AS A DECLINE. "Solar reached a record 22 percent of the mix", "installations fell by a fifth", "the IEA expects strong growth".
Pa1.frame_elements.F2c.does_not_fire_when: The number has no direction. By itself, "Wind produced 132 TWh" fires nothing; "wind produced a record 132 TWh, up a fifth" fires F2c.
Pa1.frame_elements.F3a.fires_when: The paragraph refers to carbon, greenhouse gases, emissions, climate targets, or the effect of the technology on the climate.
Pa1.frame_elements.F3b.fires_when: The paragraph situates the technology within — or as a barrier to — the energy transition, a coal or nuclear phase-out, or a decarbonisation pathway, WITHOUT putting forward an explicit emissions claim.
Pa1.frame_elements.F4b.fires_when: The paragraph mentions security of supply, sovereignty, geopolitical risk, or shortage presented as a matter of national security.
Pa1.frame_elements.F4b.recall_warning: A frame does NOT call for an articulated causal mechanism. "Wind strengthens Germany's energy security", without an explanation of how, triggers F4b.
Pa1.frame_elements.F5a.fires_when: The paragraph touches on intermittency, baseload, dispatchability, backup, the requirement for storage, or the question of whether power is available at the time it is needed.
Pa1.frame_elements.F5a.does_not_fire_when: Weather is portrayed with no link to power supply. On its own, "It was a still, grey week" does not trigger F5a.
Pa1.frame_elements.F5b.fires_when: The paragraph refers to transmission lines and their permitting, connection queues, grid infrastructure, curtailment, or the siting of generation relative to demand.
Pa1.frame_elements.F6a.fires_when: The paragraph refers to whether it is possible at all to build, rebuild, restart or operate the technology: technical obstacles, immaturity, irreversibility, or a physical constraint on doing so.
Pa1.frame_elements.F6a.boundary: NOT F5a. F5a is about supplying power at the time it is needed - intermittency, baseload, backup. F6a is about whether the plant can exist or operate at all. "Reaktivierung kaum mehr denkbar, weil der Rückbau fortgeschritten ist" counts as F6a, not F5a.
Pa1.frame_elements.F6b.fires_when: The paragraph mentions efficiency, yield, the potential for output, or how technically suitable a design or a site is.
Pa1.frame_elements.F6b.boundary: This is NOT F1a. F1a applies to cost per unit, while energy per unit of area, or a yield estimate, falls under F6b. Code "Cheaper per MWh" as F1a. Code "Produces more kWh per m²" as F6b. A single paragraph may trigger both.
Pa1.frame_elements.F6b.boundary_vs_F5a: Judge by the CAUSE, not the effect. If the cause is weather, season or variability, this counts as an availability claim and triggers F5a: "weak wind conditions cut the wind turbines' output by 3.2 percent" is F5a, because the wind did not blow. If the cause is the design, the site or the technology's efficiency, this counts as a performance claim and triggers F6b: "PV on noise barriers yields X kWh/m2" is F6b. Both are triggered when the text makes both claims.
Pa1.frame_elements.F7a.fires_when: The paragraph refers to the amount of land or space the technology requires, or to competition with alternative uses of that land.
Pa1.frame_elements.F7b.fires_when: The paragraph touches on the visual appearance of the technology in the landscape, on noise, on local acceptance or resistance, or on a conflict over siting.
Pa1.frame_elements.F8a.fires_when: The paragraph in question refers to planning law, legal classification, approval procedures, regulatory facilitation, or regulatory burden.
Pa1.frame_elements.F8a.boundary: NOT F5b. F5b constitutes permitting of GRID infrastructure — transmission lines, connection queues. F8a constitutes the legal and administrative treatment of the generating installation itself.
Pa1.frame_elements.F9.fires_when: A framing function is clearly carried out that none of F1a-F8a captures.

Pa2.technologies.nuclear.definition: Counted as a low-carbon COMPARATOR despite not being a renewable technology.
Pa2.technologies.storage.definition: The SUBJECT of the statement is batteries, pumped hydro, and other storage.
Pa2.frame_elements.F1a.does_not_fire_when: A number is present that does not represent a price. Quantities such as installed capacity in megawatts, output in terawatt-hours, or a count of turbines are NOT classified as a cost claim.
Pa2.frame_elements.F1b.fires_when: The paragraph mentions subsidies, feed-in tariffs, levies, auctions, public funding, tax credits, or addresses the issue of who bears the cost of deployment.
Pa2.frame_elements.F2b.fires_when: The paragraph refers to investment, industrial capacity, factory or project decisions, exports, supply chains, or national competitiveness.
Pa2.frame_elements.F2c.fires_when: The paragraph presents a deployment, output or market figure AS GROWTH, AS A RECORD, or AS A DECLINE. "Solar reached a record 22 percent of the mix", "installations fell by a fifth", "the IEA expects strong growth".
Pa2.frame_elements.F2c.does_not_fire_when: The number does not indicate a direction. By itself, "Wind produced 132 TWh" activates nothing; "wind produced a record 132 TWh, up a fifth" activates F2c.
Pa2.frame_elements.F3a.fires_when: The paragraph refers to greenhouse gases, carbon, emissions, climate targets, or the impact of the technology on the climate.
Pa2.frame_elements.F3b.fires_when: The paragraph situates the technology within — or as a barrier to — the energy transition, a coal or nuclear phase-out, or a decarbonisation pathway, WITHOUT explicitly stating an emissions claim.
Pa2.frame_elements.F4a.fires_when: The paragraph refers to reliance on, or lack of reliance on, energy imports, a foreign supplier, or a named exporting country.
Pa2.frame_elements.F4b.fires_when: The paragraph mentions security of supply, sovereignty, geopolitical risk, or shortage presented as an issue of national security.
Pa2.frame_elements.F5a.fires_when: The paragraph refers to intermittency, baseload, dispatchability, backup, the need for storage, or whether power is available when it is needed.
Pa2.frame_elements.F5a.does_not_fire_when: A description of weather that is not linked to power supply does not trigger F5a. The presence of "It was a still, grey week" by itself is insufficient to activate F5a.
Pa2.frame_elements.F5b.fires_when: The paragraph mentions grid infrastructure, connection queues, transmission lines and their permitting, curtailment, or the location of generation in relation to demand.
Pa2.frame_elements.F6a.boundary: NOT F5a. F5a concerns providing power when required—intermittency, baseload, backup. F6a concerns whether the plant can exist or operate at all. "Reaktivierung kaum mehr denkbar, weil der Rückbau fortgeschritten ist" is F6a, not F5a.
Pa2.frame_elements.F6b.boundary: NOT F1a. Cost per unit qualifies as F1a; energy per unit of area, or a yield estimate, qualifies as F6b. "Cheaper per MWh" is F1a. "Produces more kWh per m²" is F6b. A paragraph may trigger both.
Pa2.frame_elements.F6b.boundary_vs_F5a: Focus on the CAUSE, not the outcome. If the cause lies in weather, season, or variability, classify as an availability claim and trigger F5a: "weak wind conditions cut the wind turbines' output by 3.2 percent" is F5a, because the wind did not blow. If the cause lies in the design, the site, or the technology's efficiency, classify as a performance claim and trigger F6b: "PV on noise barriers yields X kWh/m2" is F6b. Both F5a and F6b are triggered when the text includes both types of claims.
Pa2.frame_elements.F7a.fires_when: The paragraph mentions the amount of land or space required by the technology, or refers to competition with alternative uses of that land.
Pa2.frame_elements.F7b.fires_when: The paragraph refers to the technology's appearance in the landscape, to noise, to local acceptance or opposition, or to a siting conflict.
Pa2.frame_elements.F8a.fires_when: The paragraph refers to approval procedures, legal classification, planning law, regulatory burden, or regulatory facilitation.
